title: Cheeblest and the Sister of Storms
subtitle: Book Three of the Castle Everstair stories

characters.name: Shock
characters.sheet: Shock: a tall slender girl, a head taller than the other sisters, always standing very straight; long storm-grey hair falling past her waist; a long charcoal-grey hooded cloak whose hem fades into soft mist; grey gloves; her whole face hidden behind a smooth dark carved mask shaped like a gently scowling storm-cloud creature with two small carved fangs at its frown, round dark eye-holes, a thin hairline crack down one cheek, and a small simple tipped-sideways crescent moon — one clean thin C-shaped curve — scratched above the brow; the mask never comes off and no part of her face is ever visible; unsettling but gentle, never gory or horrific.

cover.imagePrompt: Cover: Cheeblest small and brave in the foreground, standing on the great glowing castle stair with her purple dress and black bows caught in the wind, looking out across a deep dark sea at a vast soft grey storm swirling above the distant tall black tower — and faint within the storm-swirl, the barest suggestion of a dark mask shape; warm gold light from the castle windows behind her. Open sky in the upper third for the title.

questions: Shock wears a mask all the time, even when nobody is looking. Why do you think somebody might want to hide?
Evilest saw the shiny new world Shock wanted to build, and she didn't want it. What was missing from it?
Moon didn't fight the storm. She just looked at Shock's dream — and didn't look away. Why do you think that made the storm stop?
The friends keep a bowl of warm soup waiting for the stormy sister. If she ever knocked on the door, what would you say to her?
lookAndFind: Shock's mask has a tiny tipped-over crescent moon scratched above the brow — can you find it? And keep watch for doors in places where doors don't belong.

spreads.title: The silence
spreads.text:
Nobody spoke when the summer was done.
Nobody spoke — not a single one.
For out on the water, as still as a stone,
stood somebody masked, and she stood all alone.

She looked at them once through the holes in her mask.
She didn't want soup. She had nothing to ask.
She turned, and she walked on the sea like a floor,
and the tower — their tower — swung open its door.
spreads.imagePrompt: Quiet night at the rock pool moments after summer's end: far out on the flat moonlit sea, the tall masked sister walking away across the water's surface toward the distant black tower, whose main door stands open glowing faint violet; in the foreground at the pool's edge, Moon, Baby Lady, the young jaguar cub and Cheeblest stand close together, very still, watching her go. Full bright moon, calm sea, hushed.

vocab.definition: a pretend face someone wears over their real one

spreads.title: Locked out
spreads.text:
By morning the tower was taller. It's true.
And it hadn't asked anyone. Towers don't do
the things this one did: it had grown, overnight,
a crown of new doors at a dizzying height.

And down on the sand stood the sisters, locked out —
locked out of the home they'd been scary about.
Evilest hammered and hollered, "IT'S ME!"
The door didn't budge. It was waiting, you see.
spreads.imagePrompt: Soft grey morning on wet black sand: the dark stone tower grown strangely taller overnight, sprouting a crown of many small mismatched doors where its windows used to be; at its base Evilest hammering on the big shut main door, crown askew, mid-holler, while Beedlist stands perfectly still beside her, hands folded. Silver morning light, unsettling but gentle.

spreads.title: Doors don't open for strangers
spreads.text:
Across the wide water the friends saw it all:
the mask on the sea, and the tower grown tall.
"Who is she?" asked Moon. Cottontail didn't know:
"I've sailed every somewhere a sailboat can go,

and nobody, nowhere, wears masks on the sea."
Then Cheeblest said, quietly, "Listen to me.
Doors don't open for strangers. It knew her. It did.
I lived my whole life there —

and it never swung open like that once for me."
spreads.imagePrompt: Morning at the warm rock pool: Moon, Baby Lady and the young jaguar cub gathered close around Cheeblest, who looks out across the wide grey-blue sea toward the distant grim black stone tower silhouetted dark against the sky, its many new doors faintly visible; worried small faces, warm golden light from the castle behind them, the pool glowing gently; a small pale perfectly round full moon in the sky (never a crescent).

spreads.title: The secret the tower kept
spreads.text:
Inside, up a stairway as new as the day,
the sisters found halls that had not been that way,
and there stood the masked one, so still and so tall,
and her voice, when it came, was like snow. That was all.

"Sisters," she said. "I'm your sister. I'm Shock.
I was born in this tower. I'm older than talk.
And nobody told you. Not once. Not a peep.
I'm the secret this tower was built here to keep."

And Evilest lit up spike after spike:
a BIGGER, more terrible sister! Her like!
She bowed till her crown nearly swept at the floor:
"Whatever you're planning — I'm yours. Tell me more."

But Beedlist said nothing. She stayed in the black.
She looked at the mask. And the mask looked back.
spreads.imagePrompt: Inside the tower, a vast new hall of pale grey stone lit warmly by tall candelabras: the tall masked sister standing very straight at the center; Evilest delighted, grinning wide, mid-bow with her spiky crown nearly sweeping the floor; Beedlist far back in soft shadow, perfectly still, watching the mask. Unsettling but gentle, warm candlelight against grey stone.

vocab.definition: something you know but keep hidden away

spreads.title: The un-stitching
spreads.text:
Then Shock climbed her tower and stood at the crown,
and the sky went the grey of a storm sitting down,
and she reached up and pinched, very gently, like thread —
and a stone of the stair floated up from its bed.

Then two stones. Then ten. Like puzzle-bits, slow,
they drifted up out of the place stones should go.
And thin as an eyelash, far up past the blue,
a crack crossed the moon. And the crack was new.

"I'll stop," said the mask, in her snowfall voice,
"when you bring me the shines. All three. It's a choice.
This world came out wrong. I will take it apart,
and build a new world in the shape of my heart."
spreads.imagePrompt: The tall masked sister completely alone — no other people or children anywhere in the scene — standing at the very top of the tower beneath a huge, slow, soft grey storm-swirl; far across the water, glowing golden stones of the great castle stair drifting gently up into the sky like floating puzzle pieces; high above, a thin hairline crack across the bright, perfectly round full moon. The scene stays luminous: moonlight, warm stair-glow, soft violet sky.

vocab.definition: a thin line where something has started to break

spreads.title: Coming loose
spreads.text:
How do you fight with the weather? You don't.
You can ask it to stop, but it probably won't.
They watched their dear stair come undone, bit by bit,
like somebody slowly unbuttoning it.

The stones didn't fall. Nobody was hurt.
They rose, soft as bubbles, away from the dirt,
and they hung in the sky, and they didn't make sound.
And a quiet that's wrong is the loudest thing round.
spreads.imagePrompt: Seen from the castle side: Moon, Baby Lady, the young jaguar cub and Cheeblest small at the foot of the great stair as several of its glowing stones float calmly upward around them like golden bubbles; the children holding each other and gazing up; grey sea, heavy soft sky, everything lit warm gold by the floating stones.

vocab.definition: opening something slowly, one little button at a time

spreads.title: The storm and the cat
spreads.text:
Then the storm came for Cottontail's power. It pried.
It circled her, sniffing. It hunted. It tried.
It turned out her pockets — no pockets. It blew
through her fur and her whiskers. No magic came through.

"I keep telling everyone," said the wet cat,
"there isn't a shine under this, under that.
My claws are just claws. They grew where they stay.
You can't take a thing that won't come away."

And the storm went quite still, for it didn't know what
to do with a something that couldn't be got.
spreads.imagePrompt: On the wet sand in the wind: the young jaguar cub standing firm and unbothered as soft ribbons of grey storm-wind curl all around her, ruffling her fur and pink hair and finding nothing to take; she holds up one paw showing small ordinary claws, her face calm and almost amused; warm moonlight breaking through the grey. No other animals.

vocab.definition: the long soft hairs on an animal's cheeks
poked and pulled, trying to get something open

spreads.title: The givers
spreads.text:
But Moon and her sister sat close on the stair,
by the space where a step had gone off in the air,
and they thought the same thought, and they thought it as one
(they have never once argued — not ever, not yet):
"She can have every shine. She can have every sun.
A world full of friends is the best you can get."

So they filled up their arms with their shimmer and glow
and set off for the tower to give it away.
And the storm, up above, watched them come. And you know
that a storm shouldn't smile. But it did, in its grey.
spreads.imagePrompt: Night: Moon and Baby Lady walking together along the shore toward the distant tower, arms and paws full of glowing gold, silver and pink light, faces gentle and determined; ahead, the grim black stone tower, its big door slowly opening; grey storm sky above, the carried light glowing warm around them like lanterns.

spreads.title: The world she would build
spreads.text:
Meanwhile the sisters, inside, on their own,
went poking through hallways the tower had grown,
past a small dusty room where five little beds slept,
all made, very neat, like a promise half-kept,

to a door standing open a crack, silver-grey,
with the world Shock would build when this world went away:
it was tidy. It shone. It was rowed. And it gleamed.
And Evilest stopped. For she knew it. She'd dreamed:

a room full of crowns and a very tall chair,
and nobody, nobody, nobody there.
She looked a long look. Then she said, very small,
"I don't think I want to be queen, after all."
spreads.imagePrompt: Inside the tower: Evilest and Beedlist at a tall grey doorway glowing silver, looking into a dream-like vision of a perfectly tidy, shining, empty world — neat rows of crowns and one very tall empty throne, beautiful and cold, nobody in it; Evilest's face fallen and small; behind them in the dim candlelit hallway, a small dusty room with exactly five little neat black beds in a row just visible — black wooden bed frames, black blankets — five beds, no more. Unsettling but gentle.

spreads.title: She won't stop
spreads.text:
They ran. Down the stairways, down two at a time,
out the door, down the sand, to the edge of the brine,
and stood in the path of the glow coming near.
"STOP," puffed out Evilest. "Keep your shine here.

She's our sister. Our oldest. And nobody knew.
Not us. Not our whole lives. I promise it's true.
And I've seen the new world she would build when it's done —
there's nobody in it. Not us. Not anyone."

And Beedlist, who never says anything, wrote
three small words in her book, and held up the note,
and the three words were these, in her smallest black pen:
"SHE WON'T STOP." And the sea went flat again.
spreads.imagePrompt: On the wet black shore before the tower door: Evilest with arms flung wide, blocking the path of Moon and Baby Lady who carry armfuls of glowing light; beside her Beedlist holds up a small open black book, its page showing only tiny unreadable pen marks; urgent but tender faces, storm-grey sky, the children lit warm by the carried glow.

spreads.title: The girl who knew towers
spreads.text:
Then Cheeblest walked forward, alone, up the sand,
past sisters, past friends, holding nobody's hand,
and she stood at the foot of the tower, head high,
in her bows, very small, looking up at the sky,

and she called to the mask at the top of it all:
"I know about towers! I lived in one too!
You hide till the hiding is all that you do!

I had a small dream and I hid it away —
and somebody looked at it anyway. SEE?
Moon! Do the thing that you once did for me!
Don't run! Don't give! Don't fight her! Just LOOK!"
spreads.imagePrompt: Small brave Cheeblest standing alone at the foot of the huge tower, bows and purple dress tugged sideways by the wind, head high, calling up toward the tiny masked figure at the tower's distant top far above — Cheeblest is completely alone on the shore, no other people or children anywhere in the scene except the tiny masked figure far above; grey storm light warmed by gold from the castle far across the sea; above, a perfectly round full moon bearing a thin hairline crack (never a crescent).

vocab.definition: all by yourself, with nobody beside you

spreads.title: The looking
spreads.text:
So Moon set her armful of shine on the sand,
and took Baby Lady's soft paw in her hand,
and she closed her eyes gently, and looked the long way —
past the mask, past the storm, past the grey, past the grey.

And deep at the middle of all of that weather
she found one small dream, folded up like a letter,
and the dream wasn't thunder, and it wasn't rain,
and it wasn't a world crumbled small. It was plain:

somebody looking at her, and then —
not looking away. Just looking again.
spreads.imagePrompt: Dream-vision spread with soft dissolving edges, framed in swirling gentle storm-grey clouds: inside a hushed grey room where all the mirrors are draped with white sheets, a small girl seen only from behind as a soft dark silhouette, face never visible, standing before a door open just a crack with warm golden light spilling through toward her. Tender, hushed, glowing, kind.

vocab.definition: a written message you fold up and send to someone

spreads.title: Not beaten, not finished
spreads.text:
And high on the tower, the storm lost its spin,
and the stones hung as still as the night they were in.
"Stop looking at me," said the mask, low and thin.
And Moon said, quite gently, "I already did.

I can't see your face, and I won't even try.
But I saw you. I saw you. You're not very hid."

And Shock — who could crumble a world into sand —
took one step away, like a wave leaves the land,
and stepped through a door that was suddenly there,
and the door closed behind her. And storm became air.

Not beaten. Not finished. Not sorry. Not done —
just gone for tonight, like a storm. Or a sun.
spreads.imagePrompt: The storm holding its breath at first pale gold of dawn: floating golden stair stones hanging motionless in the sky; on the tower top, the tall masked sister stepping backward through a tall grey freestanding door, her cloak trailing into mist, the door half closed behind her; far below, Moon watches gently with one hand slightly raised; a pale perfectly round full moon fading in the dawn sky (never a crescent). Quiet, soft, luminous.

vocab.definition: all at once, when you weren't expecting it

spreads.title: The missing step
spreads.text:
The stones settled home like slow flakes of snow,
each back into place in the stair's even row —
all but one step, near the ninety-ninth bend,
that never came down. There's a gap there, my friend.
They hop it. You'd hop it. It isn't so far.
But it's how they remember that somewhere, storms are.

And the crack on the moon knitted shut, thin and slow,
the way that a scrape on your knee learns to go —
though on some very clear nights, you can find a faint line,
like the moon has a secret. (It does. It's fine.)

And the tower shrank back to its everyday frown,
and it kept one new door that it didn't take down.
spreads.imagePrompt: Soft pink dawn: the great glowing stair rebuilt as the last golden stones settle down into place like slow snowflakes — one single gap where a step is missing, and Moon, Baby Lady, the young jaguar cub and Cheeblest all hopping over the gap together mid-step, laughing; above, the fading moon with the faintest thin healed line across its face. Joyful, warm, light.

vocab.definition: grew back together, bit by bit, like stitches

spreads.title: Soup, crowded
spreads.text:
That night at the table there wasn't much room.
Two extras had followed them home through the gloom:
one girl with a crown, sitting cross-armed and proud,
who said that the soup was "just fine" — but quite loud;

one girl all in black, who said nothing at all,
who wrote in her book with her back to the wall,
one word at a time, very neat, in between
small sips of her soup. (What it said, we've not seen.)

And the bowl for the stormy one? Full. Set. Still there,
with its steam going up by the one empty chair.
Nobody talked of it. Everyone knew.
Some bowls you keep setting. It's just what you do.
spreads.imagePrompt: Cozy warm interior at night: a round wooden table crowded with seven bowls of steaming soup under golden lamplight — Moon, Baby Lady, Cheeblest and the young jaguar cub squeezed in happily, Evilest — a little girl the same size and age as the other children, not an adult — seated with arms crossed but staying, and Beedlist, also a small girl, writing in a small black book between sips; every character is a small child — and one empty chair with a full steaming bowl waiting in front of it; crescent moon carved above the door; through the window, a small perfectly round full moon in the night sky (the sky moon is never a crescent).

vocab.definition: feeling big and pleased about yourself

spreads.title: The storm on the horizon
spreads.text:
And later, at bedtime, when lamps were all low,
Moon looked from her window, out where the waves go,
and there on the line where the sky meets the foam,
a little grey storm paced. It didn't come home.

It didn't come closer. It didn't quite go.
It walked the horizon, slow, to and fro,
the way you might pace at a door in the night
when you almost could knock. When you can't. When you might.

And Moon raised her hand to the glass. And it's true:
she waved at the storm. Like you do. Like you do.
The storm didn't wave back. (A storm has no hand.)
But it stopped its slow pacing, out there past the land,

and it stayed, very still, all the rest of the night.

And down in the warm room, asleep in her chair,
the jaguar was dreaming of salt and sea air,
and out on the tip of one ordinary claw,
a tiny shine flickered that nobody saw.

Not borrowed. Not gifted. Not stolen. Not new.
It grew there, the way that her claws had grown too.

A shine of her own. Her very first one.
It was small. It was hers. It had only begun.
spreads.theEnd: The End — of the third one.
spreads.imagePrompt: Quiet night, seen from inside a warm dim candlelit room: Moon at a tall arched castle window, one hand raised to the glass in a small wave toward the sea — far out on the moonlit horizon, a small soft grey storm-swirl standing perfectly still on the water — and in the foreground, the young jaguar cub fast asleep curled in a cozy armchair, one front paw draped over the armrest with a tiny warm golden shine glowing on the tip of one small claw, unnoticed. Hushed, tender, silver sea, one warm candle.

vocab.definition: the far-away line where the sky touches the sea
glowed on and off, like a tiny candle
